newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU animal feed industry seeks BSE-safe bone meal.
newsitem.headline: EU animal feed industry seeks BSE-safe bone meal.

text.p: Safety of meat, bone meal and all other animal feed ingredients was of prime importance in protecting animal and public health against mad cow disease, the European Feed Manufacturers' Association (FEFAC) said.
In a statement issued during an EU scientific conference on meat and bone meal, FEFAC said that scientific experts must confirm that the use of meat and bone meal is safe.
An veterinary inspectors must ensure that meat rendering plants respect EU safety standards.
"The compound feed manufacturer will then only buy from such controlled and certified rendering plants," FEFAC said, adding that purchasing and consumption records should be kept.
The conference, organised by the European Parliament and European Commission, is expected to recommend food safety policy options.
Infected meat and bone meal is believed to be the main cause of the fatal cattle brain disease, known medically as Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), which has ravaged mainly British herds.
Britain's admission in March 1996 that the disease might be transmitted to humans eating infected beef, triggered a massive health scare and resulted in an EU ban on British beef exports.
